title: On-call SDK cheat pouch — quickpatch & triage playbook (draft)
content:
Goal:
A compact, highly actionable "cheat pouch" for oncall engineers and integrators when SDK-related incidents hit production. Focus is emergent fixes, short repros, and telemetry queries — not deep design docs. Meant to live in Drive + link to PR templates and runbooks.

Audience:
- SRE / oncall engineers handling Redwood API/Dedicated/Private SDK failures
- Developer-experience engineers triaging customer SDK issues
- Solutions engineers doing quick field fixes for pilots

Scope (what this covers):
- Fast triage checklist for SDK requests that cause latency/regressions/errors
- Minimal reproducible test steps (curl + SDK snippets) for hosted API + Dedicated fallbacks
- Telemetry queries to check common failure signals (latency, 5xx spikes, KV cache misses)
- Quickpatches: environment toggles, config rollbacks, or temporary mitigations
- Communication templates and escalation points

What this intentionally excludes:
- Full design proposals (link to RFCs instead)
- Long-term fixes — add to backlog and reference a ticket

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Safety check: Is this customer-facing severity P0/P1? If P0, page SRE lead and start the incident channel.
2) Identify surface area: Hosted API vs Dedicated pool vs Private VPC.
3) Is there an obvious rate-limit or quota error? Check the token-level quotas dashboard.
4) Check model routing fallbacks: did a variant switch cause a quality/latency change?
5) Gather reproducible example (minimal prompt + headers) to reproduce locally or via curl.

Immediate data to collect (commands/snippets):
- curl to reproduce generation call (hosted API):
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
    -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-70b", "input":"<short repro prompt>", "max_tokens":64}'

- Node quick repro using official SDK (inline snippet):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-llama-70b', input: '<short repro prompt>' });

- For Dedicated: reproduce with pool endpoint + include route headers: REDWOOD_POOL_ID and X-Route-Policy

Telemetry quick hits:
- Prometheus/Loki example queries (replace <service> with api/dedicated-runtime):
  - 5xx rate: rate(http_requests_total{service="<service>",status=~"5.."}[5m])
  - P95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="<service>"}[5m])) by (le))
  - KV cache hit ratio (approx): sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])))
  - Recent deploys: label_replace(kube_deployment_status_replicas_updated{namespace="redwood"}, "deploy", "$1", "deployment", "(.*)")

Common failure patterns & quick mitigations:
- Spike in latency after model variant rollout:
  * Mitigation: rollback to previous model variant (console -> model routing -> revert) or enable auto-fallback to smaller variant. Notify product.
- High error rates from embedding endpoint after quantization change:
  * Mitigation: revert quantization config for affected model in Dedicated, add an overlay config to route to verified model.
- Auth-related 401s for a customer but other customers OK:
  * Mitigation: check API key mapping, recent token rotations, KMS errors. If key revoked, provide temporary token or escalate IAM.
- Excessive tokens / unexpected cost spike:
  * Mitigation: temporarily rate-limit the customer at the API gateway; enable sampling for debug.

Quickpatch recipes (minimal, reversible):
- TTL / cache bypass for reproducing: set REDWOOD_BYPASS_KV=true on the repro test to force cold path
- Disable prefix caching for suspect flows: in route config, flip "prefix_cache_enabled" -> false for the route (console)
- Force model fallback: set X-Prefer-variant: fallback-small in request header (temporary)
- Autoscaler pause: in Dedicated console, set autoscaler.min_replicas = current to stop noisy scaling during triage (SRE action)

Micro-repro playbook (local):
1) Start a minimal local stub with REDWOOD_STUB_MODE=1 (use SDK stub package — reference repo in linked_artifacts).
2) Replay the exact headers + body captured from production.
3) Toggle REDWOOD_BYPASS_KV and measure latency difference; this isolates cache vs runtime kernel issues.

Safety & guardrails when patching:
- Always test quickpatch in staging before production when possible (5–10 min smoke).
- Document the exact change in the incident channel and add a rollback step.
- Mark any customer-affecting temporary fix with TTL (e.g., auto-revert in 60m) to force follow-up.

Communication templates (copy into Slack/incident):
- Initial post:
  "Incident: SDK errors impacting <customer> — started <timestamp>. Triage underway. Repro: <short snippet>. Telemetry shows p95 latency up X%. Paging SRE lead @<name>. Temporary mitigation: disabled prefix cache on route <route-id> (auto-revert in 60m)."
- Follow-up when fixed:
  "Resolved: root cause <short>. Rollback applied at <timestamp>. Follow-up ticket: JIRA-RI-XXXX for permanent fix and postmortem."

Post-incident follow-ups (owner checklist):
- Create a JIRA with steps to permanent fix and link back to incident channel
- Add an end-to-end test that covers the repro path (SDK + tiny integration)
- Add a telemetry alert to catch regression earlier
- If fix touches SDK surface, open a PR with a changelog and a migration note for integrators

Proposed short-term SDK improvements (quick wins):
- Add a lightweight "diagnostic" flag to SDKs (sdk.diagnostic = true) that sends verbose telemetry for a single request id and TTL=1h
- Expose a one-liner that toggles KV-bypass in the SDK for repro runs
- Ship a small CLI: redwood-sdk-repro --endpoint <url> --headers "k:v" --body <file> to reproduce calls quickly in CI/staging

Open questions / outstanding risks:
- Do we need a signed short-lived debug token flow for customer debug sessions? (security review needed)
- Can we safely expose cache-bypass controls in hosted API without opening DoS vectors?
- Owner for CLI utility (DE or infra)?

TODOs (near-term):
- [ ] Draft PR for SDK diagnostic flag (owner: Marco) — target: 2-week sprint
- [ ] Prototype redwood-sdk-repro CLI (owner: Jenna) — target: spike this week
- [ ] Add alert for KV miss ratio > 20% sustained over 5m (owner: SRE team)
- [ ] Link this doc in team oncall binder and Confluence after review

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep the pouch intentionally small. If this grows, split into: rapid-ops (oncall) vs SDK-dev (features).
- When pushing CLI/flags, add strict rate limits and auditing.

References and quick links:
- SDK repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482
- Incident runbook index (Confluence): confluence://internal/runbooks/oncall
- Telemetry dashboards: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/sdk-quick-ops

Last edits: 2025-10-02 — added KV miss ratio query + CLI TODOs.

If you're reading this during a page: start a thread, copy the reproducer into the incident channel, and ping the DE triage rotation. Keep notes here for the postmortem.
